comment: Shared test vectors for the contact form.
The rules live in two independent implementations: packages/contact/src/index.ts, which
runs in the browser, and apps/contact-php/src, which runs on the server and never trusts
the browser. Independent must not mean different: a reader told their message is fine and
then told by the server that it is too long has been lied to once.
Both implementations run these vectors. packages/contact/src/index.test.ts does it for the
browser side and apps/contact-php/tests/ParityTest.php for the server side, so a divergence
fails a build instead of reaching a reader.
Each vector names what it is for. 'errors' lists the field and problem pairs in the order
the implementations must report them; an empty list means the submission is accepted, and
'submission' then says exactly what the trimmed values must be.

vectors.name: an emoji counts as two, because the browser counts code units
vectors.comment: A subject of 119 ordinary characters plus one emoji is 121 code units, so it is one over the limit of 120. Counting characters instead of code units would accept it in one implementation and refuse it in the other.
